question: A corporate trainer uses a personal Max plan for her own course-design work. Her manager asks her whether her Claude conversations are being used to improve Anthropic's models. What should be her first step?
options: A) Assume that they are, because conversations on personal plans always feed model improvement work.
B) Ask her manager to raise it with Anthropic, as only the vendor can answer that question.
C) Check her own model improvement privacy setting, since on a personal plan the choice is hers.
D) Assume that they are not, because Anthropic never trains on customer data on any plan at all.
correct_answers: C) Check her own model improvement privacy setting, since on a personal plan the choice is hers.
explanations: Consumer plans are not automatically in scope for model improvement. It is a user-controlled setting, so assuming the worst gives her manager an answer that may simply be wrong.
Escalating to the vendor is unnecessary for something visible in her own account settings, and it leaves the manager waiting for an answer she could give today.

Correct. On Free, Pro and Max the user chooses whether their conversations may be used to improve Claude, so the honest answer depends on how her own setting is configured. Checking it is a step she can take herself and it produces a factual answer rather than an assumption.

This states the commercial position, where inputs and outputs are not used for training by default, and applies it to a personal plan. The consumer and commercial rules are different and must not be conflated.
